html:
The Tawakoni are a Southern Plains people closely related to the Wichita, speaking a Wichita language of the Caddoan family. In the 1700s they lived in farming villages, first along the Arkansas River in Oklahoma and later on the Brazos and Trinity rivers in Texas, growing maize and hunting bison.

They traded with French Louisiana, fought the Spanish and the Osage, and lived near the Waco, a related band whose village grew into the city of Waco. Tehuacana in Texas carries their name. Pushed out by American settlers, they were moved to Indian Territory in 1859. Today they are enrolled in the Wichita and Affiliated Tribes of Oklahoma, alongside the Caddo.
